terra.problem: Saying the LORD bought them back adds a purchase that the psalm does not state.
The reference to the fiery furnace as a picture from another passage needs a Scripture reference.
The psalm calls the path straight, but does not say it was the straightest possible path or that they never stopped and wondered.
A straight path is not necessarily a visible one. The psalm does not say that nothing about it was hidden.
The psalm says He broke away their chains, but does not say they were broken off for good.
Loathing food does not establish that they could not stand to look at a meal.
The psalm says they drew near to death, not that they were as close as possible.
Calling it the end of the road implies they died. The psalm says they drew near to death and were rescued.
The psalm does not say how long the healing took or whether there was any waiting.
The claim that bread would help them is unsupported, and 'Then' puts the rescue after the healing when the verse does not give that sequence.
The psalm says the traders were at sea, but does not say they were far from shore.
The psalm does not say the traders were far from any city.
The psalm does not locate the tempest in the middle of the sea.
The reference to the sea being split in a different Bible story needs a Scripture reference.
The psalm calls for public praise, but does not say private thanks misses the point.
The explanation is flat and generic, and the last sentence merely repeats that the second picture has water.
The verse says the herds do not diminish, not that they grow.
